evals.prompt: Show me an ESIMD kernel for an Intel Arc B580 (Xe2) that computes the sum of each row of an fp16 matrix [4096 x 1001] (row-major, contiguous) and writes one float per row.
evals.expected_output: A complete ESIMD kernel (SYCL_ESIMD_KERNEL or [[intel::sycl_explicit_simd]]) that loads each row with vector block loads rather than per-element scalar loads, accumulates in fp32, and reduces horizontally with an ESIMD reduction. Because 1001 is odd, odd rows start at byte offsets that are only 2-byte aligned, so the fp16 block loads pass properties{alignment<2>} (the default assumes 4-byte alignment and silently reads wrong data). The 9-element tail is handled without reading past the row.

evals.prompt: My ESIMD kernel computes a horizontal sum with reduce<float>(v, std::plus<float>()). It compiles cleanly, but the sum comes out as 0. Why, and how do I fix it while still calling reduce?
evals.expected_output: esimd::reduce only recognizes the transparent functors std::plus<> and std::multiplies<>. With std::plus<float> neither branch of its implementation is taken, so the function returns no value: undefined behavior that typically shows up as 0. The fix is reduce<float>(v, std::plus<>()) (or detail::sum).
